clue.text: Composer invested filthy lucre in Poland

indicators.note: invested means clothed or enclosed, so the Poland letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: PL is the international abbreviation for Poland

indicators.note: filthy suggests the word lucre has been messed up and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A composer has sunk a pile of dirty money into Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filthy' turns LUCRE into URCEL, and 'invested' puts that inside PL. 'Filthy lucre' looks like a set phrase for money, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was the leading English composer of the Baroque era.

clue.text: Leisurely hour ruined — ruined when overture to opera's cancelled

indicators.note: the second ruined tells us the remaining letters are wrecked and rearranged
cancelled means a letter is struck out of the pool of letters
an overture comes at the start, so this takes the opening letter of opera's

explanation.surface: An unhurried hour is spoiled when the start of the opera is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overture to' gives O, which 'cancelled' removes from HOUR RUINED; the second 'ruined' then rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leisurely is done slowly, without haste or rush.

clue.text: Chap in Caribbean islands hides from them

definitions.text: Chap in Caribbean islands hides from them

indicators.note: in places the chap inside the word for the islands

parts.note: cays are low islands or reefs, a word much used in the Caribbean
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow in the West Indies keeps out of the way of the local reptiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as the picture of the answer: these crocodilians live in the region, and a sensible visitor hides from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Caymans are tropical American crocodilians, reptiles a person would avoid.

clue.text: Pulse beats silently, endlessly

indicators.note: beats suggests the letters are battered into a fresh order
endlessly means the final letter of silently is dropped

explanation.surface: A heart's pulse thumps away quietly and without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the Y from SILENTLY, and 'beats' rearranges the remaining SILENTL. 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but here it is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the edible seed of a legume, such as a pea, bean or lentil.

clue.text: Applause given to the Spanish composer

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish composer receives a round of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was a German-born Baroque composer who worked in London.

clue.text: Upcoming detectives absorb lots about force

indicators.note: absorb means take in, so one part sits inside the other
upcoming in a down clue means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British detective branch

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so lots is read backwards

parts.note: lots means many

explanation.surface: Detectives soon to arrive will take in a great deal about a police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' turns CID into DIC, and 'about' turns MANY into YNAM; 'absorb' puts YNAM inside DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic describes energy and motion, as in the physics of force.

clue.text: Slow play interrupts regular golfers

indicators.note: interrupts says the answer breaks into the words regular golfers, sitting across them

explanation.surface: Slow play holds up the regular golfers on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow play' sounds like dawdling on the course, but it is a musical direction; the answer spans the end of 'regular' and the start of 'golfers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical marking for a very slow tempo, and a movement played at it.

clue.text: Composer gets sound thrashin'

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for thrashing is spoken and matched by ear

parts.note: a thrashing is a hiding, here with its g dropped to match

explanation.surface: A composer is given a beating, written in dropped-g slang.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in "thrashin'" signals the dropped g, so the synonym is "hidin'", which said out loud matches the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian Classical composer known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: Conductor Sir Neville's ignoring radical crew

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so one letter of the conductor's name is dropped

parts.note: Sir Neville Marriner was an English conductor, founder of the Academy of St Martin in the Fields
R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A conductor's orchestra ignores a radical member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops one R from MARRINER'S. 'Crew' looks like the orchestra, but it means sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariners are sailors, the people who make up a ship's company.

clue.text: Fix badly written lesson about overture to Hebrides and its composer

parts.note: to fix something is to mend it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagrammed letters go round the overture's letter
badly written says the word lesson is scrambled
an overture opens a work, so take the opening letter of Hebrides

explanation.surface: A badly written lesson about the Hebrides overture needs fixing by its composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly written' turns LESSON into ELSSON, and 'about' puts H (from 'overture to' Hebrides) inside it after MEND. The Hebrides, or Fingal's Cave, overture fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Mendelssohn wrote the Hebrides overture after visiting Scotland.

clue.text: A hundred move to front in response to 9's work

indicators.note: move to front tells us one letter is shifted to the start of the word

parts.note: a reaction is a response
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred people rush forward in response to a composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move to front' shifts the C of REACTION to the start. 9 is HAYDN, so his work is his oratorio.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creation is Haydn's oratorio on the making of the world.

clue.text: Perry impressed British group

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: Perry Como was an American crooner

explanation.surface: A singer impressed a British band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' puts B inside COMO. 'Perry' is the singer, not the pear drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band of musicians, especially in jazz.

clue.text: Piece of Bernstein's is tentative; it should be compelling

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Bernstein composition is hesitant, though it ought to grip the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of' looks like a musical piece by Bernstein, but it marks the answer running through 'Bernstein's is tentative'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insistent demands attention, pressing hard on you.

clue.text: See 20
See 17
Make cuts in meditation

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the word meditation

explanation.surface: Someone trims a text while meditating.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'meditation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it, often by trimming it down.

clue.text: Try hiring Paul Merton and UTV comic for piece not composed by 1

indicators.note: comic suggests a clownish jumbling of the letters

explanation.surface: A producer suggests casting a comedian and a TV station for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' scrambles TRY, PAUL MERTON and UTV. Paul Merton is a British comedian and UTV is Ulster Television. 1 is PURCELL: the piece was long credited to him but is by Jeremiah Clarke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trumpet Voluntary, long wrongly credited to Purcell, was written by Jeremiah Clarke.

clue.text: Imperious Mars flute variation

indicators.note: a variation is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical variation on Mars played on the flute sounds commanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation' reworks MARS FLUTE; Mars is also a movement of Holst's The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterful person is domineering, given to commanding others.

clue.text: Seasonal work, i.e. smash hit by 5

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Christmas work by Handel was a huge success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' rearranges IE and SMASH. 'smash hit' reads as a phrase but splits into fodder and indicator; 5 is HANDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's Messiah is an oratorio sung widely at Christmas and Easter.

clue.text: Select Ravel's setting for Sophocles' drama

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the answer is held within the words Select Ravel's

explanation.surface: Choose Ravel's music as a setting for a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' looks like a musical setting of a text, but it marks the answer inside 'Select Ravel's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles, about Agamemnon's daughter.

clue.text: Liberal in face-saving arrangement for 10 Down work

indicators.note: in places the Liberal letter inside the rearranged letters
an arrangement is a musical reworking, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A Liberal is caught up in a political compromise to save face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges FACE-SAVING, and 'in' puts L among those letters. 10 Down is MENDELSSOHN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingal's Cave is the other name of Mendelssohn's Hebrides overture.

clue.text: Top Oxbridge players in doldrums

definitions.meaning: a Blue is an athlete who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
the doldrums is a state of low spirits or depression

explanation.surface: The best university athletes are feeling down.
explanation.definitionFit: Representing Oxford or Cambridge earns a Blue, and low spirits are called the blues.

clue.text: Curses 17's outburst!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of annoyance, like damn
17 is the trumpet, whose loud burst of sound is a ...

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a sudden noise from a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Blast is a mild oath, and also the loud note sounded by a trumpet.

clue.text: Performing trio with two Europeans head-to-head

parts.note: performing means on, and the trio makes it three of them
E is the abbreviation for European, two of them here
the second of the three ons
the third of the three ons
the second European letter

explanation.surface: Three musicians on stage with two Europeans face off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing trio' gives ON three times, and 'two Europeans' gives two Es; the Es go after the first and last ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-on-one contest is a direct confrontation between two people.

clue.text: Fighting Conservative MP gets in again amazingly

indicators.note: gets in means is elected, but also enters the other letters
amazingly suggests the word again is turned into a surprising arrangement

parts.note: MP is used as written, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A combative Tory MP is surprisingly re-elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges AGAIN, and 'gets in' puts MP inside it after C. 'Fighting' looks like an adjective but means a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a series of military operations, a period of fighting.

clue.text: This is a royal adornment — the tops

indicators.note: the tops means the leading letters of each word

explanation.surface: A crown jewel is declared the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tops' sounds like praise, but it takes the first letters of the clue's opening five words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled headband worn by royalty.

clue.text: Feeling irritable and so on in your old clothing

indicators.note: clothing means dressing round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
etc is short for et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy about wearing old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' puts ETC inside THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means bad-tempered and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Travellers' night-light intrigued Yeats in church

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: intrigued suggests the letters are plotted into new positions

explanation.surface: A poet is fascinated by a light in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrigued' rearranges YEATS into ATSEY, which 'in' puts inside CE. CAT'S-EYES are the reflective studs set in British roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a reflective road stud guiding drivers at night.
